reason: The cited evidence confirms that a bcc HEA with homogeneous elemental distribution exhibits superconductivity (E1, E2), but none of the passages provide any data or analysis linking configurational entropy to electron–phonon coupling, nor do they compare ordered vs. disordered states. The core mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: High configurational entropy maintains a uniformly disordered, homogeneous bcc structure in the HEA.
This uniform disorder optimizes electron–phonon coupling.
Reducing atomic-scale randomness (e.g., by chemical ordering) diminishes electron–phonon coupling.
Diminished coupling lowers the superconducting transition temperature (Tc).
The untreated high-entropy state exhibits a higher Tc and robust Type II superconductivity compared to a more ordered state.
